Sample.evidence_source: The present study comprised 155 participants, 44 males and 111 females.

Mean age of participants.evidence_source: Participants' ages ranged between 18 and 35, with males and females' mean ages presenting significant differences, but of small size effect, as indicated by Cohen's d value (t(153) = 2.20; p = 0.03; d = 0.36). Specifically, males' mean age (M = 22.36; SD = 3.14) was slightly higher than women's mean age (M = 21.30; SD = 2.54).

Percentage of college or higher of parti.evidence_source: The sample presented a mean of years of schooling of 13.69 (SD = 1.63), which did not differ significantly between males and females (t(153) = −0.81; p = 0.42).

Mean BMI of participants.evidence_source: Concerning body mass index (BMI), participants reported a mean of 22.63 (SD = 3.57), which corresponds to a normal-weighted sample (WHO, 1995). Participants' BMI means were different between men (M = 23.54; SD = 3.14) and women (M = 22.28; SD = 2.99).

Assessment of BMI.evidence_source: Concerning body mass index (BMI), participants reported a mean of 22.63 (SD = 3.57) — indicating BMI was obtained via participant self-report.

Number of studies.evidence_source: Text refers to 'The present study comprised 155 participants...' indicating a single study.

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes one study (referred to as 'the present study', not labeled as 'Study 1') with 155 participants (44 males, 111 females) aged 18–35. Males were slightly older than females (M=22.36 vs. 21.30) and had a slightly higher BMI (M=23.54 vs. 22.28); overall mean BMI was 22.63. Mean years of schooling was 13.69 (SD=1.63); reported sex differences in age and BMI were statistically significant but of small effect size.
